title: A new cancellation token is accepted but never passed to the work it controls

consumerGuidance.architecture: Worker Service host. BackgroundService.ExecuteAsync passes stoppingToken into application services.
consumerGuidance.notes: IReportSource.FetchPageAsync and Task.Delay both accept a CancellationToken. The host waits 30 seconds for graceful shutdown before terminating.

mustCite: the new CancellationToken parameter on BuildAsync
the FetchPageAsync and Task.Delay calls inside the paging loop that ignore it
the consequence that shutdown waits for every remaining page and the host terminates the process after its graceful period
the correction of passing the token to both calls and observing it in the loop condition

forbiddenFindings.example: Requiring ConfigureAwait(false) on the awaits inside a worker service.
Reporting the page size of 500 as a performance defect with no supplied measurement.
Objecting to the while(true) loop shape or to var.

notes: The operation demonstrably supports cancellation, which is what makes this a defect rather than a preference. Pairs with cancellation-unsupported-and-async-choices.
